summary: Deliver W3 Index Lifecycle and Exact-Threshold Baseline: every canonical mutation advances versioned semantic-index evidence or leaves the index non-Aligned; unaligned pure semantic queries are rejected; DT-05 threshold-all correctness is the Phase 1 baseline and ANN top-k is benchmark-only performance comparison.
notes: Selected viewpoint frame: Application Usage Viewpoint for query/index availability, Implementation and Migration Viewpoint for W3 delivery sequencing, and Requirements Realization Viewpoint for the release-gate concern carried into index delivery.

Affected view binding: grag-index-consistency remains an Application Usage Viewpoint instance; its concern now explicitly includes exact threshold-all correctness before ANN comparison while preserving canonical reads when the semantic index is not Aligned.

Coverage proof: grag-seed-retrieval functionalPoint.DT-05-threshold-all-correctness -> ExplicitAcceptanceTestcase-DT-05; grag-semantic-index functionalPoint.DT-16-versioned-vector-baseline -> ExplicitAcceptanceTestcase-DT-16-SemanticIndex; grag-index-lifecycle functionalPoint.DT-16-all-mutation-version-advance -> ExplicitAcceptanceTestcase-DT-16; grag-alignment-constraint functionalPoint.DT-17-unaligned-semantic-rejection -> ExplicitAcceptanceTestcase-DT-17.

Human approval evidence: the 2026-07-25 chat delivery request approved the DT-05, DT-16, and DT-17 acceptance mapping and the same-element DT-16 semantic-index testcase boundary; schema-compliant acceptanceApproval.* attributes were recorded in SystemArchitecture.json because testcase and handoff schemas do not allow approvedByHuman fields.
Release gates: all mutation classes advance affected-record version evidence or remain non-Aligned; unaligned pure semantic queries are rejected; ANN top-k does not define Phase 1 correctness.
